newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-HODDLE FURIOUS OVER FOWLER, MCMANAMAN WITHDRAWALS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HODDLE FURIOUS OVER FOWLER, MCMANAMAN WITHDRAWALS.

text.p: England coach Glenn Hoddle launched a stinging attack on Roy Evans on Tuesday after Steve McManaman and Robbie Fowler were withdrawn from his squad for the next five internationals.

Hoddle blasted the Liverpool boss's decision as "disappointing and frustrating," and added: "What's really disappointing is that I didn't know about the situation until after I'd announced the squad."
Fowler has been withdrawn because he needs surgery on his nose to cure a breathing problem, while McManaman has a knee problem which needs rest and recuperation.
England play a friendly against South Africa at Old Trafford on Saturday, a World Cup qualifier against Poland on May 31 and three matches in the Tournoi de France in June.
"We knew Steve's knee was a problem but we thought Robbie's operation could have been put off," said Hoddle.
"You can bet I have had some conversations with Roy Evans in the last 48 hours -- and you know that sometimes there has to be a bit of give and take in medical situations.
"Steve's knee problem has been a long-term one and he does probably need some rehabilitation on it.

"But Robbie's operation could have been done at a different time. He's not played the last three games of the season for Liverpool because of suspension. If he had undergone the operation when he was suspended, he could have been eligible for the Poland game and maybe even fit enough to play in it.
"This could stop Robbie playing in the World Cup in 12 months time. As one door shuts for one player, another opens for someone else."
Hoddle has called up Manchester United's Andy Cole and John Scales of Tottenham as replacements and Hoddle is now keen to take Cole to the tournament in France.

"The people in the squad now have a very good opportunity to stake their claim, especially if they are in the squad for a longer period than usual and Andy Cole will now have the opportunity that Robbie had," said Hoddle.

England will also be without Les Ferdinand, Gary Pallister and Paul Merson through injuries, while Paul Gascoigne's place in the starting line-up is still in some doubt although he trained with the squad on Tuesday.
